items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: Bill Price was very much influenced by Louis and Bunk and possibly some of the others like George Mitchell.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. In the early 40s, I think. I can't remember. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And what you know about Johnny what you know about Johnny, then you took off of records, except maybe what you read. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. But your style derived from what you would hear on records. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, entirely. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Any of the other boys in that group make an effort to emulate the New Orleans men? Now I'm talking about the University of Chicago group.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, I think Bill Price did. Bill Price was very much influenced by Louis and Bunk and possibly some of the others like George Mitchell.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Bill Price now lives in Minneapolis, but frequently comes to Chicago and he hears about a jam session where he might sit in. So he comes down sometimes for a Sunday session where there is advertised there will be ten bands. Well, he knows that if he comes down there enough people know him that he'd get in one of those bands. So he's on and on for a set or two. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I understand that he works occasionally in Minneapolis, becoming a friend of Doc Evans and other...
